before.jp: 道が悪いのでスピードを出せない。

structure_explanation.en: The sentence has two parts linked by the causal conjunction ので ('because, since'): the cause 道が悪い ('the road is/are bad'), in which 道 is the subject marked by が and 悪い is the い-adjective predicate; and the result スピードを出せない ('I can't get up speed'). 出せる is the potential form of 出す ('to put out, get out'), here negated as 出せない ('I can't / it won't'), with スピード ('speed') as the object marked by を. In ので, the の nominalizes the clause and the で comes from the copula.

Em ので, o の nominaliza a oração e o で vem da cópula.

structure_explanation.en: Here there is a relative clause modifying ところ: [道が２つの小道に分かれる] ('the road splits into two paths') describes which ところ ('point/place'). The whole clause + ところ becomes the destination marked by へ of the verb 来た ('we came/arrived', past of 来る). Important note: ところ here is the concrete noun 'point/place' modified by a relative clause, and NOT the grammatical aspectual ところ (about to/doing/just did) that was the target; so the target structure does not apply.

The structure 動物の中には...もいる means 'among animals, there also exist (some)...'; もの ('being/thing') refers back to 'those (animals) that are carnivorous', and いる indicates the existence of living beings.

A estrutura 動物の中には...もいる significa 'entre os animais, também existem (alguns)...'; もの ('ser/coisa') retoma 'os (animais) que são carnívoros', e いる indica a existência de seres vivos.
